bull.b: Sustained, large QoQ and YoY Atruvio growth demonstrates durable commercial traction and expanding patient uptake. This revenue base can fund scale, enable operating leverage as fixed costs are spread, and underpins management's path to breakeven while supporting launches of additional pipeline assets.

A ~95% gross margin signals strong unit economics for product sales in ATTR and related specialty medicines. High gross margins create a durable buffer to absorb SG&A and R&D spending, improving the company’s ability to translate higher sales into operating leverage and eventual profitability over time.

The large preferred equity raise materially improves liquidity and reduces near-term refinancing risk, providing permanent capital to fund commercialization and multiple planned launches. This structural funding supports execution of the commercial strategy and lowers the immediacy of dilution from near-term equity raises.

bear.t: Large ongoing cash burn and negative FCF
bear.b: Persistent negative operating and free cash flow indicate the business remains cash‑consumptive absent sustained commercial scale. Continued burn elevates dependency on external financing, risks dilution, and constrains discretionary investment if revenues slow or launch costs run higher than planned.

A sizable negative equity balance reflects accumulated losses and weak capital buffer, reducing financial flexibility. Over time this increases refinancing and covenant risk, may limit partner or payer confidence, and can force suboptimal financing choices if operational performance falters.

Heavy dependence on a single commercial product concentrates execution and access risk: payer decisions, diagnostic bottlenecks, or competitive entrants could materially affect revenues. Durable risk remains until additional pipeline approvals and launches materially diversify the revenue base.
